To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the evidence for the health benefits of moderate alcohol consumption is compelling but not definitive, and that the best way to resolve the remaining questions about the effects of moderate alcohol consumption on chronic disease is through a long-term clinical trial.

(i) randomized trials are possible in a variety of complex nutritional areas, and (ii) the execution of a long-term randomized trial of moderate alcohol consumption on chronic disease risk is possible, but would require careful planning and a large, collaborative research effort.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a long-term randomized clinical trial of moderate alcohol consumption on chronic disease.
the development of a long-term randomized trial to test the hypothesis that moderate alcohol consumption is causally related to risk of chronic disease.
the potential of alcohol to prevent and/or treat chronic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence to support a recommendation that moderate alcohol consumption is beneficial or harmful to health, although the possibility that such consumption is harmful cannot be excluded.
there is no evidence that moderate alcohol consumption is either harmful or beneficial for chronic disease prevention.
moderate alcohol consumption is not a cause of coronary heart disease, and may be a cause or preventer of diabetes or breast cancer, or may have no effect on these diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided the rationale for the conduct of a randomized clinical trial to test the effects of moderate alcohol consumption on the risk of chronic diseases and discussed key features to maximize the value of such a trial.

moderate alcohol intake is associated with lower risk of cardiovascular diseases, diabetes and breast cancer, although the mechanisms are not clear and the causal nature of the associations has yet to be proven.
moderate alcohol intake has been associated with a reduced risk of coronary heart disease (CHD), diabetes and breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time is right to consider a full-scale, randomized trial of moderate drinking and health.
a full-scale randomized trial of alcohol consumption and chronic disease can be designed, and that it would be a valuable contribution to the evidence base for the role of alcohol in chronic disease.
the time has come to move beyond observational studies and start a long-term randomized trial of moderate drinking and chronic disease.
